instance (L : MutexLayout) (adm : List Nat) (s : SC) (reg : SyncReg) (c g : Nat) :
    Decidable (NewMutexPreBase L adm s reg c g) :=
  decidable_of_iff (OptP (s.A[g]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
      ∃ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, y.holder = .place q ∧ s.flat.Usable q) False ∧
    (s.view c).ExercisableAt g .modify ∧ ControlOf L s ⟨g, none⟩ ≠ none ∧
    OptP (s.A[g]?) (fun y => y.origin ≠ none → ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length,
      y.holder = .place q → ∀ l ∈ y.footprint, l ∉ footprint s.P q ∧
        ∀ r ∈ List.range s.P.length, OwnedIn s.P q r → l ∉ footprint s.P r) False ∧
    (∀ e ∈ reg, e.Live s → e.guarded ≠ g) ∧ g ∉ adm ∧ NoCoveringDesc s g) <| by

    refine ⟨?_, b, c, ?_, e, f, h⟩
    · unfold OptP at a ⊢; split at a <;> simp_all
      obtain ⟨-, -, q, -, hq⟩ := a; exact ⟨q, hq⟩
    · unfold OptP at d ⊢; split at d
      · intro ho q hq; exact d ho q (List.mem_range.2 (by
          rename_i y hy
          sorry)) hq
      · exact d
  · sorry

end Ern.Concurrency

p='Ern/Concurrency/SyncLib.lean'

s=s.replace("\nend Ern.Concurrency\n",'''
/-! ## Theorem 1, last part: `SyncAuthorized` and `deriveSync` without live entry (WC2 C14, C24) -/

/-- Theorem 1 (WC2 C14, C24): in a state whose registry has no live entry, the obligation of WC2
C14 makes `K_C.SyncAuthorized` false. Fragment: every state, single-context ones included. -/
theorem syncAuthorized_false {kc : KC} {reg : SyncReg} {s : SC} (hsound : SyncSound kc reg s)
    (hnone : ∀ e ∈ reg, ¬ e.Live s) (g f : Nat) : ¬ kc.SyncAuthorized s g f := fun h => by
  obtain ⟨e, he, -, hl⟩ := hsound g f h
  exact hnone e he hl

/-- Theorem 1 (WC2 C15, C24): in a state whose registry has no live entry, under the obligation
of WC2 C14, `deriveSync` is never enabled. -/
theorem conservative_deriveSync {kc : KC} {reg : SyncReg} {s : SC} (hsound : SyncSound kc reg s)
    (hnone : ∀ e ∈ reg, ¬ e.Live s) (c g : Nat) (s' : SC) : ¬ DeriveSyncStep kc s c g (.ok s') :=
  fun ⟨_, h⟩ => syncAuthorized_false hsound hnone g _ (Guarded.ok_iff.1 h).1.authorized

/-! ## Theorem 6: exclusivity of grants (Spec 1 §50; WC2 C15) -/

/-- An ancestor of an authority whose origin is `g` is `g` or below `g` (Spec 1 §42, §49.5). -/
theorem ancs_le_origin {t : S3} (hw : WF3 t) {b g : Nat} {y : Authority} (hy : t.A[b]? = some y)
    (hyo : y.origin = some g) {x : Nat} (hx : x ∈ t.ancs b) : x ≤ g := by
  have hgb : g < b := hw.origins b y g hy hyo
  have horg : t.org b = some g := by simp [S3.org, hy, hyo]
  rw [S3.ancs, chain_cons horg hgb] at hx
  rcases List.mem_cons.1 hx with rfl | hx
  · exact Nat.le_refl _
  · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hx)

/-- Theorem 6 (Spec 1 §50, I1; WC2 C15, C21.2): two distinct active authorities of own mode
`Modify` whose origin is the same `guarded` and whose footprint is `footprint(guarded)`, nonempty,
cannot coexist. Fragment: states satisfying `WF3` and `I1` on the globally live frames. -/
theorem grants_exclusive {s : SC} (hw : WF3 s.flat) (h1 : I1 s.flat) {g a b : Nat}
    {x y : Authority} (hab : a ≠ b) (hx : s.A[a]? = some x) (hy : s.A[b]? = some y)
    (xa : x.active = true) (ya : y.active = true) (xm : x.mode = .modify)
    (xo : x.origin = some g) (yo : y.origin = some g)
    (xf : ∀ l, l ∈ x.footprint ↔ l ∈ s.flat.afp g) (yf : ∀ l, l ∈ y.footprint ↔ l ∈ s.flat.afp g)
    {l : Nat} (hl : l ∈ s.flat.afp g) : False := by
  have hga : g < a := hw.origins a x g hx xo
  have hgb : g < b := hw.origins b y g hy yo
  have hna : a ∉ s.flat.ancs b := fun h => by have := ancs_le_origin hw hy yo h; omega
  have hnb : b ∉ s.flat.ancs a := fun h => by have := ancs_le_origin hw hx xo h; omega
  have := h1 a b x y l hab hx hy xa ya ((xf l).2 hl) ((yf l).2 hl) hna hnb
  rw [xm] at this; cases this.1

/-! ## Theorem 5: realizability (WC2 C25) -/

/-- Theorem 5 (WC2 C14, C15, C25): under `SyncInv` and `GrantDiscipline`, and the kernel invariant
re-indexed (`KInvC`: `WF3`, `I1` and `I2` are used), the library instantiation of
`SyncAuthorized` (registry and controller facts only) for the current frame of a live context
entails that no active descendant of `guarded` covers a protected leaf and all the preconditions
of `deriveSync`, in particular I1 for the full-footprint grant (§60.3) and the validity of the
origin chain (§60.1). Fragment: states satisfying `KInvC`. -/
theorem realizability {k : K} {L : MutexLayout} {reg : SyncReg} {s : SC} {c g : Nat}
    (hk : KInvC s) (hsi : SyncInv L s reg) (hgd : GrantDiscipline s reg) (hc : s.stk c ≠ [])
    (ha : LibSyncAuthorized L reg s g (s.view c).top) :
    NoCoveringDesc s g ∧ DeriveSyncPre (libKC k L reg) s c g := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hfr, hw⟩, ⟨⟨h1, h2, -, -⟩, -, -⟩, -, -⟩ := hk
  obtain ⟨e, he, rfl, hl, hn, -⟩ := ha
  have hnc := hgd e he hl hn
  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hl
  have hym : y.mode = .modify := by
    have := hsi.guarded e he ⟨y, hy, ya⟩; simp only [OptP, hy] at this; exact this.1
  have hfp : s.flat.afp e.guarded = y.footprint := by simp [S3.afp, hy]
  refine ⟨hnc, ⟨y, hy, ya⟩, ⟨e, he, rfl, ⟨y, hy, ya⟩, hn, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_, fun l h => h, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · sorry
  · exact I2.ancs_active h2 ⟨y, hy, ya⟩
  · intro l hl'
    have hl'' : l ∈ y.footprint := by rw [← hfp]; exact hl'
    exact hw.footprints _ y hy l hl''
  · intro l hl'
    have hl'' : l ∈ y.footprint := by rw [← hfp]; exact hl'
    have hd : descModes (s.view c) e.guarded l = [] := by
      apply List.eq_nil_iff_forall_not_mem.2
      intro m hm
      obtain ⟨j, z, hz, za, hlz, hanc, -⟩ := mem_descModes.1 hm
      exact hnc j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz))
        ⟨hanc, ⟨z, hz, za⟩, l, by simp [S3.afp, hz]; exact hlz, hl'⟩
    show Allows (effective (s.view c) e.guarded l) .modify
    rw [effective_eq hy ya hl'', hd, hym]
    simp [effOf, Allows, OptP, Mode.le]
  · intro b _
    unfold OptP; split
    · rename_i z hz
      intro za hnb hcov
      exfalso
      obtain ⟨l, hl', hlz⟩ := hcov
      have hb : b ≠ e.guarded := fun h => hnb (h ▸ List.mem_cons_self ..)
      have hnanc : b ∉ (s.view c).ancs e.guarded := fun h => hnb (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h)
      by_cases hdesc : e.guarded ∈ s.flat.ancs b
      · exact hnc b (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz)) ⟨hdesc, ⟨z, hz, za⟩, l,
          by simp [S3.afp, hz]; exact hlz, hl'⟩
      · have hl'' : l ∈ y.footprint := by rw [← hfp]; exact hl'
        have := h1 e.guarded b y z l (Ne.symm hb) hy hz ya za hl'' hlz hdesc hnanc
        rw [hym] at this; cases this.1
    · trivial
  · rw [SC.view]
    obtain ⟨f, rest, hf⟩ := List.exists_cons_of_ne_nil hc
    simp [S3.top, hf]

end Ern.Concurrency
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

import Ern.Concurrency.Frames

/-!
# Provisional by-value transmission at `spawn` (WC2 C5)

The composite of WC2 C5: `spawn` (WC2 C4) creating, among the locals of the new frame, a fresh
root `destination`, and the transfer of an owned `source` of the creator into it, with the
preconditions of O4 (Spec 1 §63) except the destination side of §63.1, replaced by WC2 C5.2–C5.3.

WC2 C5.4 evaluates the resulting-state conditions of O4 on the final state but does not say in
which state the other conditions are evaluated. Two of them depend on it: the source side of
§63.1 (exercisable `Modify` of the creating frame over the source, WC2 C5.1) and §63.4 (the
exemption of the grounding authority), since the spawn part moves the transmitted parameters to
the new frame. Both readings are defined (`SrcRightBefore`, `SrcRightAfterSpawn`) and
`readings_differ` exhibits a state where every other clause holds and the two readings disagree.
The composite relation itself is not defined: its definition requires that choice (see the
report).
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- Effect of the composite (WC2 C5 effect): the effect of `spawn` (WC2 C4), then the effect of
O4 (Spec 1 §63) from `src` to `dst` on the resulting state. -/
def spawnValEff (s : SC) (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) (src dst : Nat) : SC :=
  (spawnEff s c ps ls).set (transferEff (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat src dst)

/-- WC2 C5.2: `dst` is a fresh root local of the initial frame of the new context (its leaves are
`Uninit`, it holds no derived authority and its root authority is held by that frame by
construction of `spawnEff`). -/
def FreshRootLocal (s : SC) (ls : LocalShape) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ i ∈ rootIdx ls.toShape, dst = s.P.length + i

/-- Decidability of `FreshRootLocal` (WC2 C5.2). -/
instance (s : SC) (ls : LocalShape) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (FreshRootLocal s ls dst) := by
  unfold FreshRootLocal; infer_instance

/-- Clauses of the composite whose state of evaluation is fixed by WC2 C4 and C5: C4.1, C4.3,
C4.5 (Spec 1 §72.2); C5.2; the source side of §63.1 without the right (usability); §63.2, §63.3,
§63.5, §63.6 (first half) and §63.8 on the state where the destination exists, after the spawn
part; the resulting-state conditions §63.6 (second half), §63.7 and §63.9 on the final state
(WC2 C5.4). Not included: the source right of §63.1 and §63.4 (two readings below), the
resulting-state conditions of WC2 C4.5–C4.6 (state of evaluation not fixed by WC2: after the
spawn part or after the composite) and WC2 C4.6, C5.8 ("invariants hold", see the report). -/
structure SpawnValPreBase (k : K) (s : SC) (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
    (src dst : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- WC2 C4.1: the creating context and its current frame are live. -/
  creatorLive : s.stk c ≠ []
  /-- WC2 C4.3: every transmitted parameter is an active derived authority held by the creating
  frame. -/
  params : ∀ a ∈ ps, OptP ((s.view c).A[a]?) (fun y => y.active = true ∧
    y.holder = .frame (s.view c).top ∧ y.origin ≠ none) False
  /-- WC2 C4.5 (Spec 1 §72.2): the locals form a well-formed shape. -/
  localsOK : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape
  /-- WC2 C5.2: the destination is a fresh root local of the new frame. -/
  freshDst : FreshRootLocal s ls dst
  /-- WC2 C5.1 (Spec 1 §63.1): the source is usable. -/
  srcUsable : (s.view c).Usable src
  /-- WC2 C5.5 (Spec 1 §63.2): same shape of ordered subtrees. -/
  sameShape : SameShape (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src dst
  /-- Spec 1 §63.3: all source leaves are `Init`. -/
  srcInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src, (spawnEff s c ps ls).I l = .init
  /-- Spec 1 §63.3, WC2 C5.2: no destination leaf is `Init`. -/
  dstNotInit : ∀ l ∈ footprint (spawnEff s c ps ls).P dst, (spawnEff s c ps ls).I l ≠ .init
  /-- WC2 C5.5 (Spec 1 §63.3): disjoint footprints. -/
  disjoint : ¬ overlap (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src dst
  /-- Spec 1 §63.5: no in-place source leaf is pinned. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ footprint (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧
    (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat.pin l = false
  /-- Spec 1 §63.6: dependencies of the usable places following the value are valid. -/
  depsValid : ∀ x ∈ movedDeps (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat src, (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat.Active x
  /-- Spec 1 §63.6 re-indexed, WC2 C5.4: `AnchorOrder` (on `ancestorC`) in the final state. -/
  anchorOrder : AnchorOrderC (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst)
  /-- Spec 1 §63.7 re-indexed, WC2 C5.4: moved held authorities satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` (on
  `ancestorC`) in the final state. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : ∀ x ∈ List.range (spawnEff s c ps ls).A.length,
    AnchorMoves (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat src x → ∀ q ∈ List.range (spawnEff s c ps ls).P.length,
      (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).flat.Usable q →
      OptP ((spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true →
        y.holder = .place q → EffAnchorOKC (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst) x
          ((spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).flat.pframe q)) True
  /-- Spec 1 §63.8: local self-blocking prevention. -/
  noSelfLock : NoLocalSelfLock (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat src dst
  /-- Spec 1 §63.9: the destination is usable in the final state. -/
  dstUsableAfter : (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).flat.Usable dst

/-- Decidability of `SpawnValPreBase` (WC2 C5). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : SC) (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape)
    (src dst : Nat) : Decidable (SpawnValPreBase k s c ps ls src dst) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.stk c ≠ [] ∧ (∀ a ∈ ps, OptP ((s.view c).A[a]?) (fun y =>
      y.active = true ∧ y.holder = .frame (s.view c).top ∧ y.origin ≠ none) False) ∧
    ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape ∧ FreshRootLocal s ls dst ∧ (s.view c).Usable src ∧
    SameShape (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src dst ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src, (spawnEff s c ps ls).I l = .init) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint (spawnEff s c ps ls).P dst, (spawnEff s c ps ls).I l ≠ .init) ∧
    ¬ overlap (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src dst ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint (spawnEff s c ps ls).P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧
      (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat.pin l = false) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ movedDeps (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat src, (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat.Active x) ∧
    AnchorOrderC (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ List.range (spawnEff s c ps ls).A.length,
      AnchorMoves (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat src x → ∀ q ∈ List.range (spawnEff s c ps ls).P.length,
        (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).flat.Usable q →
        OptP ((spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true →
          y.holder = .place q → EffAnchorOKC (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst) x
            ((spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).flat.pframe q)) True) ∧
    NoLocalSelfLock (spawnEff s c ps ls).flat src dst ∧
    (spawnValEff s c ps ls src dst).flat.Usable dst)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, p⟩ =>
      ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, p⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, p⟩ =>
      ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, p⟩⟩

/-- Source side of Spec 1 §63.1 and §63.4 for the creating context `c` in state `t` (WC2 C5.1,
C5.4): exercisable `Modify` over the source, and no active derived authority covering a source
leaf from outside the source except some grounding authority and its origin chain. -/
def SrcRight (t : SC) (c src : Nat) : Prop :=
  HasRight (t.view c) .modify src ∧
  ∃ g ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length, Grounds (t.view c) .modify src g ∧
    ∀ j ∈ List.range (t.view c).A.length, ActiveDerivedOutside (t.view c) src j →
      RightChain (t.view c) g j

/-- Decidability of `SrcRight` (Spec 1 §63.1, §63.4). -/
instance (t : SC) (c src : Nat) : Decidable (SrcRight t c src) := by
  unfold SrcRight; infer_instance

/-- Reading (a) of WC2 C5.1, C5.4: the source clauses are evaluated in the state before the
composite. -/
def SrcRightBefore (s : SC) (c src : Nat) : Prop := SrcRight s c src

/-- Reading (b) of WC2 C5.1, C5.4: the source clauses are evaluated after the spawn part, when
the transmitted parameters are held by the new frame. -/
def SrcRightAfterSpawn (s : SC) (c : Nat) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) (src : Nat) :
    Prop :=
  SrcRight (spawnEff s c ps ls) c src

namespace TransferWitness

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Examples

/-- Statics of Spec 1 `Examples.st` with frame 0 deriving a `Modify` authority (3) over leaf 0
(Spec 1 §60). -/
def w0 : SC := SC.ofS3 (deriveEff s0 0 [0] .modify)

end TransferWitness

open TransferWitness Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Examples in
/-- The two readings of WC2 C5.1/C5.4 differ (report, problem of WC2 C5): in `w0`, context 0
spawns a context transmitting authority 3 (a `Modify` derivative over leaf 0, held by frame 0) and
moves the value of place 0 into a fresh one-leaf local (place 3) of the new frame. Every clause of
`SpawnValPreBase` holds; the source right holds before the composite (through authority 3) and
fails after the spawn part (authority 3 is held by the new frame and blocks the root of place
0). -/
theorem readings_differ : SpawnValPreBase K0 w0 0 [3] [(none, 0)] 0 3 ∧
    SrcRightBefore w0 0 0 ∧ ¬ SrcRightAfterSpawn w0 0 [3] [(none, 0)] 0 := by
  decide

end Ern.Concurrency

input.description: Prove theorem 4 (SyncInv preservation)
input.prompt:
You are fork C. Scope: the preservation half of theorem 4 of the brief: `SyncInv` and `GrantDiscipline` preserved by every labelled step `LStep k L lbl st st'` (SyncLib.lean) under the encapsulation hypothesis `Encap st lbl`, and the trace corollary over `EncapsulatedTrace`. The counterexample half (derive(guarded, Observe, footprint) by the owner disables acquire while grant = none) is done by me in Traces.lean; do not write it. Branch tip at start: commit ad8c1bf on `formal/spec2-m1` (your worktree starts from it).

Deliverable: one new module `formal/Ern/Concurrency/SyncPreserve.lean` (do NOT edit Ern.lean or any existing file; lake's glob builds it). Helpers in namespace `Ern.Concurrency.SyncPreserveAux` or `private` (forks A and B write other modules in the same namespace).

Design notes from my analysis (verify, do not trust blindly):
- GrantDiscipline alone is not inductive: `unlock` releases the grant g and sets grant := none, which re-establishes GrantDiscipline only if every active descendant of guarded covering a protected leaf is g or a descendant of g. Introduce an auxiliary invariant (e.g. `GrantSubtree L s reg`: for every live entry with grant = some g and g active, every `CoveringDesc s e.guarded j` has j = g or g ∈ ancs j) and preserve the conjunction `SyncInv ∧ GrantDiscipline ∧ GrantSubtree`. import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

/-!
# Corpus runner (test module)

A computable executor for the corpus cases of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`: the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75) and the arena operations O17–O19 of Part XIV (§76–§78), over
the library state of `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena` (§46: the kernel state `S₃` and, separately, the arena
registry). This module is a test module: no model module imports it.

* `Op`: one constructor per operation, with its arguments.
* `lstep k L o`: the outcome (§58) of `o` from `L`, computed from the decidable preconditions.
* `OpRel k L o`: the relation of the operation: the kernel relation `XStep` (§60–§75) with the
  registry unchanged; `NewArenaStep`, `IssueD`, `ResetD` (Part XIV) for the arena operations.
* `lstep_sound`: the computed outcome is an outcome of the relation, `ok`, `reject` and `fail`
  alike; `lstep_ok`: an `ok` step is a library step `LStep`.
* `lrun`, `final`, `RunsTo`: a run from `LState.init statics` (§47) whose steps are all `ok` reaches
  a library-reachable state (`LReach`) whose kernel state is reachable (`Reachable`, §57).

`newArena` consults the arena registry and no other registry (§56: `others = []`): the library
states of these runs hold no administration other than arenas.
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

/-! ## Test contracts (§48, §80) -/

/-- A test contract `K` given by lists (§48): the `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone` and
`Deallocable` sets, and the `FreeCompat` pairs; `ExternalDone` lists identities of dynamic pinning
obligations (§75). Nothing is declared disjoint; every allocation request is satisfiable. -/
structure KD where
  shared : List Nat := []
  pinned : List Nat := []
  done : List Nat := []
  dealloc : List Nat := []
  compat : List (Nat × Nat) := []

/-- The contract `K` (§48) described by a `KD`. -/
def KD.toK (d : KD) : K :=
  ⟨fun _ _ => False, (· ∈ d.shared), (· ∈ d.pinned), (· ∈ d.done), (· ∈ d.dealloc),
    fun p a => (p, a) ∈ d.compat, fun _ _ _ => True⟩

/-- Decidability of `DeclaredDisjoint` for a test contract (§48). -/
instance (d : KD) : ∀ r r', Decidable (d.toK.DeclaredDisjoint r r') :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstanceAs (Decidable False)
/-- Decidability of `SharedMutable` for a test contract (§48). -/
instance (d : KD) : DecidablePred d.toK.SharedMutable :=
  fun l => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (l ∈ d.shared))
/-- Decidability of `Pinned` for a test contract (§48). -/
instance (d : KD) : DecidablePred d.toK.Pinned :=
  fun l => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (l ∈ d.pinned))
/-- Decidability of `ExternalDone`, on obligation identities, for a test contract (§48, §75). -/
instance (d : KD) : DecidablePred d.toK.ExternalDone :=
  fun p => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (p ∈ d.done))
/-- Decidability of `Deallocable` for a test contract (§48). -/
instance (d : KD) : DecidablePred d.toK.Deallocable :=
  fun p => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (p ∈ d.dealloc))
/-- Decidability of `FreeCompat` for a test contract (§48). -/

68:theorem KD.ddSound (d : KD) : DDSound d.toK := fun _ _ h => h.elim

  reference representation), its registration by `newMutex`, `acquire`, `unlock`;
* theorem 4, counterexample without encapsulation: `derive(guarded, Observe, footprint(T))` by the
  exclusive owner makes `acquire` not enabled while `grant = none` (`acquire_blocked_by_derive`);
  the encapsulated twin enables it (`acquire_enabled`);

  instantiation of `SyncAuthorized`, violating `I1`, where `deriveSync` is not enabled
  (`realizability_needs_i1`);

  (`frames_run`), and `join` on a live context has no outcome (`join_waits`);
* two `newMutex` on two protected roots owned by the same field share one controller
  (`shared_controller`, report).

namespace Ern.Concurrency.Traces

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Examples Ern.Concurrency

/-! ## Mutex value (WC2 C12, C13) -/

/-- Statics (Spec 1 §47): `0` the mutex value `m`, `1` its field `data`, `2` its field `lock`, `3`
the protected value `T`, a root owned by `data`; every leaf `Init`. -/
def mst : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true),
   ((none, some 1, 0), true)]

/-- The reference layout (WC2 C12): `guarded` is held by the first field, the controller is the
second. -/
def L0 : MutexLayout := ⟨0, 1⟩

/-- Initial single-context state (Spec 1 §47): root authority `0` of `m` held by frame 0, root
authority `1` of `T` held by `data` (place 1). -/
def c0 : SC := SC.ofS3 (S3.init mst)

/-- The statics are well formed (Spec 1 §47). -/
theorem mst_ok : StaticsOK mst := by decide

/-- After `newMutex(guarded = 1)` (WC2 C13). -/
def reg1 : SyncReg := [⟨1, none⟩]

/-- `newMutex(1)` executed by context 0 is enabled on `c0`; its controller is place 2. -/
theorem newMutex_ok : NewMutexOk L0 [] c0 [] 0 1 (c0, reg1) ∧
    ControlOf L0 c0 ⟨1, none⟩ = some 2 :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩, by decide⟩

/-! ## Theorem 4: counterexample without encapsulation (WC2 C22) -/

/-- `derive(guarded = 1, footprint(T) = [3], Observe)` by context 0, the exclusive owner. -/
def c1 : SC := c0.set (deriveEff (c0.view 0) 1 [3] .observe)

    ¬ Encap (c0, reg1) (.kernel 0 (.derive 1 [3] .observe)) :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, _, .ok (by decide), rfl⟩, fun h => h ⟨1, none⟩ (by decide) (by decide) rfl⟩

  · have := h ⟨1, none⟩ (by decide) (by decide) rfl
    exact (by decide : ¬ NoCoveringDesc c1 1) this

    simp only [reg1, List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at he
    subst he

/-- Registry after `acquire` (WC2 C16): the grant is authority 2. -/

theorem acquire_enabled : AcquireOk K0 L0 c0 reg1 0 0 (c2, reg2) :=
  ⟨by decide, ⟨1, none⟩, rfl, by decide, by decide, rfl⟩

/-- State after `unlock` (WC2 C17). -/
def c3 : SC := c2.set (releaseEff (c2.view 0) 2)

/-- `unlock` is enabled after `acquire` (WC2 C17). -/
theorem unlock_enabled : UnlockOk L0 c2 reg2 0 0 (c3, reg1) :=
  ⟨by decide, ⟨1, some 2⟩, 2, rfl, by decide, rfl, by decide, by decide, rfl⟩

/-- An encapsulated trace `newMutex`, `acquire`, `unlock` from `c0` with an empty registry (WC2
C13, C16, C17, C22). -/
theorem mutex_trace : EncapsulatedTrace K0 L0 (c0, [])
    [.newMutex 0 1 [], .acquire 0 0, .unlock 0 0] (c3, reg1) :=
  .cons trivial (.newMutex newMutex_ok.1) <|
  .cons trivial (.acquire acquire_enabled) <|
  .cons trivial (.unlock unlock_enabled) .nil

/-- `c0` with an extra active root `Modify` authority over `T` held by frame 0, unrelated to

def bad : SC := { c0 with A := c0.A ++ [⟨.modify, none, [3], .frame 0, true⟩] }

    ¬ DeriveSyncPre (libKC K0 L0 reg1) bad 0 1 := by
  have hl : ∀ {i : Nat} {e : SyncEntry}, reg1[i]? = some e → i = 0 ∧ e = ⟨1, none⟩ := by
    intro i e h
    cases i with
    | zero => simp [reg1] at h; exact ⟨rfl, h.symm⟩
    | succ i => simp [reg1] at h
  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_, by decide, fun h => ?_, by decide⟩
  · intro e he _; simp only [reg1, List.mem_singleton] at he; subst he; decide
  · intro e he _ g hg; simp only [reg1, List.mem_singleton] at he; subst he; cases hg
  · intro e he _; simp only [reg1, List.mem_singleton] at he; subst he; decide
  · intro i j e e' hi hj _ _ _; rw [(hl hi).1, (hl hj).1]
  · intro e he _ _; simp only [reg1, List.mem_singleton] at he; subst he; decide
  · have := h 1 2 ⟨.modify, none, [3], .place 1, true⟩ ⟨.modify, none, [3], .frame 0, true⟩ 3
      (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) rfl rfl (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    cases this.1

/-! ## Frame transitions (WC2 C4, C6–C8) -/

/-- Context 0 enters a call frame (frame 1) without parameter nor local (Spec 1 §72). -/
def f1 : SC := enterEffC c0 0 [] []
/-- From frame 1, context 0 spawns context 1 (frame 2, parent 1) with one local (place 4) (WC2
C4). -/
def f2 : SC := spawnEff f1 0 [] [(none, 0)]
/-- Frame 1 exits; context 1 is reparented to frame 0 (WC2 C6). -/
def f3 : SC := exitEffC f2 0
/-- Context 1 terminates (WC2 C7). -/
def f4 : SC := termEffC f3 1

/-- A run of frame transitions (WC2 C4, C6–C8): `enterFrame`, `spawn`, `exitFrameC` (reparenting
context 1 from the exiting frame 1 to its caller 0), `terminate`, `join`; each state satisfies the
frame structure `FramesC` re-indexed from Spec 1 §49.1 (checked where decidable: parents). -/
theorem frames_run : opStepC K0 (.enter [] []) 0 c0 (.ok f1) ∧ SpawnStep f1 0 [] [(none, 0)] (.ok f2) ∧
    f2.ctxParent 1 = some 1 ∧ opStepC K0 .exit 0 f2 (.ok f3) ∧ f3.ctxParent 1 = some 0 ∧
    TermStep K0 f3 1 (.ok f4) ∧ JoinStep f4 0 1 (.ok f4) := by
  refine ⟨⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, by decide,
    ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, by decide, ⟨by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩, .ok (by decide) ?_⟩
  decide

/-- WC2 C8 (brief: waiting is a non-enabled transition): while context 1 is live, `join` has no
outcome. -/
theorem join_waits : ∀ o, ¬ JoinStep f3 0 1 o := by
  intro o h
  cases h with
  | ok _ hd => exact (by decide : ¬ OptP (f3.C[1]?) (fun x => x.life = .done) False) hd

/-- `ancestorC` across contexts after `spawn` (WC2 C3): the creating frame 1 and the base frame 0
are ancestors of the initial frame 2 of context 1; after `exitFrameC`, frame 0 still is. -/
theorem ancestry : f2.ancestorC 1 2 ∧ f2.ancestorC 0 2 ∧ ¬ f2.ancestorC 2 1 ∧
    f3.ancestorC 0 2 ∧ ¬ f3.ancestorC 1 2 := by decide

/-! ## Two entries sharing a controller (report, WC2 C12 and C13) -/

/-- Statics: the mutex value `m = {data, lock}` and two protected roots `T₁`, `T₂` both owned by
`data`. -/
def mst2 : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true),
   ((none, some 1, 0), true), ((none, some 1, 0), true)]

/-- Initial state: root authorities 1 (of `T₁`) and 2 (of `T₂`) are both held by `data`. -/
def d0 : SC := SC.ofS3 (S3.init mst2)

/-- WC2 C12 requires distinct controller associations for different mutex instances; the
preconditions formalized from WC2 C13 accept `newMutex(1)` then `newMutex(2)`, and both entries
have the same positional controller (place 2). -/
theorem shared_controller : NewMutexOk L0 [] d0 [] 0 1 (d0, [⟨1, none⟩]) ∧
    NewMutexOk L0 [] d0 [⟨1, none⟩] 0 2 (d0, [⟨1, none⟩, ⟨2, none⟩]) ∧
    ControlOf L0 d0 ⟨1, none⟩ = some 2 ∧ ControlOf L0 d0 ⟨2, none⟩ = some 2 :=
  ⟨⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩, ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩, by decide, by decide⟩

end Ern.Concurrency.Traces

are ancestors of the initial frame 2 of context 1; after `exitFrameC`, frame 0 still is. -/

    f3.ancestorC 0 2 ∧ ¬ f3.ancestorC 1 2 := by decide

`data`. -/

  [((none, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true), ((some 0, none, 0), true),

preconditions formalized from WC2 C13 accept `newMutex(1)` then `newMutex(2)`, and both entries
have the same positional controller (place 2). -/

  ⟨⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩, ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl⟩, by decide, by decide⟩

theorem framesC_of {s : SC} (h0 : OptP (s.C[0]?) (fun x => x.life = .live ∧ x.parent = none) False)

    (hp : ∀ f ∈ s.frames, OptP (s.parC f) (fun g => g ∈ s.frames ∧ g < f) True) : FramesC s := by
  have hlt : ∀ c, s.Live c → c < s.C.length := fun c hc => by

  have := hp f hf; rw [hg] at this; exact this

    (spawnValEff w0 0 [3] [(none, 0)] 0 3).I 3 = .init := by
  decide

end Ern.Concurrency
''',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
Ce qui est fait sur `formal/spec2-m1` :

- **Audit des axiomes** : `reachable_kinv` et les 442 théorèmes de `Main` et `Preserve/*` n'utilisent que `{propext, Quot.sound}`. Les trois preuves par `Classical.byContradiction` ne servent qu'à 31 théorèmes de `Rename` et `StaticsConf`, que le jalon 1 ne réutilise pas. Je ne me suis donc pas arrêté après l'audit.
- **Modules compilés et commités** : `Context`, `Frames`, `Conservativity`, `Sync`, `SyncLib`, `Transfer` et `Traces`. Les 306 théorèmes existants sont tous dans `{propext, Quot.sound}`. Il n'y a ni `sorry` ni `native_decide`, et `lake build` passe sans avertissement.
- **Théorème 1** : il est prouvé pour O1–O16. Les issues coïncident une à une avec la Spec 1 sur les états à un contexte. `ancestorC` coïncide avec §39. Tout état atteignable de la Spec 1 entre dans ce domaine. Sans entrée de synchronisation vivante, `deriveSync` n'est jamais habilitée.
- **Théorème 5** : il est prouvé, mais avec en plus l'invariant noyau ré-indexé `KInvC`. Un contre-exemple vérifié montre qu'il est faux sous `SyncInv ∧ GrantDiscipline` seuls : sans I1, `deriveSync` n'est pas habilitée.
- **Théorème 6** : il est prouvé.
- **Contre-exemple du théorème 4** : il est construit. La dérivation `Observe` par le propriétaire bloque `acquire` alors que `grant = none`, et le jumeau positif l'habilite.
- **Problèmes de la candidate déjà relevés** :
  - « invariants » listés parmi les préconditions (C4.6, C5.8) ;
  - état d'évaluation d'O4.1 et d'O4.4 dans le `spawn` par valeur : un témoin `decide` montre que les deux lectures divergent ;
  - issue de `join` sur un identifiant inconnu ;
  - C12 exige des contrôleurs distincts, mais C13 ne le garantit pas : témoin avec deux mutex sur le même contrôleur ;
  - plusieurs clauses de C13, C17, C18 et C21 sans contenu formel.

**Pas encore fait :**
- **Agents en cours** : trois agents travaillent en parallèle dans des worktrees isolés. Ils prouvent la préservation (théorème 2) hors sortie de frame, le reparentage avec `exitFrameC` et `terminate` (théorème 3), et la préservation de `SyncInv` et `GrantDiscipline` sous `EncapsulatedTrace` (théorème 4).
- **Rapport** : il est rédigé (audit, passages, problèmes, décisions, écarts). Il n'est pas encore dans `formal/reports/spec2-m1.md`, faute des sections sur les théorèmes 2–4.

Je fusionne leurs modules et je finalise le rapport à leur retour.

Le composite `spawn` par valeur n'est pas défini tant que ses deux lectures ne sont pas tranchées. Sa préservation est donc ouverte, et les théorèmes 2–4 restent non vérifiés tant que les agents n'ont pas rendu leurs résultats.

<result>Fork B: theorem 3 (reparenting, OB-C13) and theorem 2 for `exitFrameC` and `terminate`. All targets are proven, nothing is open.

**Where.** `formal/Ern/Concurrency/Reparent.lean`, commit `0ec5594` on branch `worktree-agent-a9df1b08eb590751f`. I fast-forwarded the branch to ad8c1bf first, because the worktree had started at d0c2d87. No existing file was touched and Ern.lean was not edited, so you need to add `import Ern.Concurrency.Reparent` when you merge. The lake glob already builds the module. `lake build` passes with no warnings, there is no sorry/admit/axiom/native_decide/noncomputable, and all 64 theorems of the module depend only on `{propext, Quot.sound}`. I checked that with a module-scoped `collectAxioms` script: `scratchpad/forkB/AuditR.lean`.

**Public theorems** (namespace `Ern.Concurrency`, with `s`, `c`, `k` implicit):

- **Live frames and ancestry, `exitEffC_ancestorC`.** Hypotheses: `FramesC s` and `(s.stk c).tail ≠ []`. Conclusion:
  - `y ∈ (exitEffC s c).frames ↔ y ∈ s.frames ∧ y ≠ (s.stk c).headD 0`;
  - for `g`, `y` live after the step: `(exitEffC s c).ancestorC g y ↔ s.ancestorC g y`.
- **Same for `terminate`, `termEffC_ancestorC`.** Hypotheses: `FramesC s`, `(s.stk c).length = 1`, `s.ctxParent c ≠ none`.
- **Frame structure kept, `exitEffC_framesC`.** `FramesC (exitEffC s c)`, under the same hypotheses as `exitEffC_ancestorC`.
- **Same for `terminate`, `termEffC_framesC`.** Needs `c ≠ 0` in addition to the `terminate` hypotheses.
- **Reparenting target, `exitEffC_reparent` and `termEffC_reparent`.**
  - `s.parC f = some p`, so `p` is the immediate parent of the exiting frame `f`, not an arbitrary ancestor.
  - Every context live after the step gets `ctxParent d = if s.ctxParent d = some f then some p else s.ctxParent d`.
- **Kernel effect, `exitEffC_kernel` and `termEffC_kernel`.**
  - `A` and `D` equal `(exitEff (s.view c)).A` and `.D`.
  - `P`, `I`, `dead`, `pins` and `nF` are unchanged.
  - So reparenting changes only `C`.
- **Theorem 3, `exitFrameC_anchorOrder`.** From `FramesC s`, `WF3 s.flat`, `AnchorOrderC s` and an `ok` step `opStepC k .exit c s (.ok s')`, it gives `AnchorOrderC s' ∧ AnchorOrderHeldC s'`.
- **Theorem 3, `terminate_anchorOrder`.** The same for `TermStep k s c (.ok s')`.
- **Theorem 2, `exitFrameC_preserves` and `terminate_preserves`.** From `KInvC s`, `RootHeldConv s.flat` and `HeldAnchored s.flat`, an `ok` step gives `KInvC s' ∧ RootHeldConv s'.flat ∧ HeldAnchored s'.flat`. The two auxiliaries are used only for their own conjuncts; the `KInvC` part needs `KInvC s` alone (`ReparentAux.Pop.kInvC`).

**How it is built.** The shared structure `ReparentAux.Pop` describes "pop the top frame `f` of `c`, reparent to `p`" and both steps instantiate it. Under it, the parent chain after the step is the chain before with `f` filtered out, which gives the ancestry result.

For `AnchorOrderC` I adapted Spec 1's `exit_anchorOrder` to `ancestorC`. That needed one extra fact the linear proof never uses: the holder frame of the surviving root anchor is itself a live frame after the step. It comes from `Frames.exit_root_survives`.

`WF3`, `Inv3base`, `NoDangling` and `RootHeldConv` reuse Spec 1's `Frames.exit_*` lemmas on `s.view c`, bridged to the new flat state by membership congruence. `HeldAnchored` follows the exit case of Spec 1's `op_preserves_heldAnchored`.

**Watch out.** `List.getElem?_modify`, `getElem?_modify_eq` and `getElem?_modify_ne` depend on `Classical.choice`. I replaced them with a local `ReparentAux.getElem?_modify'`. Forks A and C will hit the same thing if they rewrite the context list.

**Definitions and WC2.** I found no problem with C6 or C7, and no definition needed changing. One observation: `exitFrameC` can never reparent its own context's initial frame, because under `FramesC` that frame's parent is smaller than every frame of its stack. The proof gets this for free through the `repO` form.

I did not check how this module interacts with the files forks A and C are writing, or whether merging leaves duplicate helper names in the namespace.</result>

import Ern.Concurrency.Conservativity

/-!
# Reparenting at frame exit and context termination (WC2 C6, C7; OB-C13)

`exitFrameC` (Spec 1 §73 re-indexed with the reparenting of WC2 C6.3) and `terminate` (WC2 C7):

* the frame structure after the step (`FramesC`), and the extended ancestry of the surviving
  frames, which is the ancestry before the step with the exiting frame skipped
  (`exitEffC_ancestorC`, `termEffC_ancestorC`);
* Theorem 3 (OB-C13): both steps preserve `AnchorOrderC` and `AnchorOrderHeldC`, and change `A`
  and `D` exactly as the effect of Spec 1 §73 (`exitEffC_A_D`, `termEffC_A_D`); reparenting
  targets the immediate surviving parent (`exitEffC_reparent`, `termEffC_reparent`);
* Theorem 2 restricted to these steps: `KInvC` and the auxiliaries `RootHeldConv`,
  `HeldAnchored` of Spec 1 on the globally live frames are preserved (`exitFrameC_preserves`,
  `terminate_preserves`).
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

namespace ReparentAux

/-! ## Lists -/

/-- Blockwise sublists give a sublist of the concatenation (WC2 C3). -/
theorem termEffC_ancestorC (hfr : FramesC s) (hone : (s.stk c).length = 1)
    (hpar : s.ctxParent c ≠ none) {g y : Nat} :
    (y ∈ (termEffC s c).frames ↔ y ∈ s.frames ∧ y ≠ (s.stk c).headD 0) ∧
    (g ∈ (termEffC s c).frames → y ∈ (termEffC s c).frames →
      ((termEffC s c).ancestorC g y ↔ s.ancestorC g y)) :=
  ⟨(termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).mem_frames hfr.nodup,
   (termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).ancestorC hfr⟩

/-- WC2 C6.3 (OB-C13): `exitFrameC` reparents exactly the live contexts whose initial frame had
the exiting frame as parent, to the immediate surviving parent of the exiting frame (its caller),
and changes no other parent. -/
theorem exitEffC_reparent (hfr : FramesC s) (hcall : (s.stk c).tail ≠ []) :
    s.parC ((s.stk c).headD 0) = some ((s.stk c).tail.headD 0) ∧
    ∀ d, (exitEffC s c).Live d → (exitEffC s c).ctxParent d =
      if s.ctxParent d = some ((s.stk c).headD 0) then some ((s.stk c).tail.headD 0)
      else s.ctxParent d :=
  ⟨(exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hcall).pf, (exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hcall).par⟩

/-- WC2 C6.3, C7 (OB-C13): `terminate` reparents exactly the live contexts whose initial frame
had the terminated initial frame as parent, to the immediate parent of that frame. -/
theorem termEffC_reparent (hfr : FramesC s) (hone : (s.stk c).length = 1)
    (hpar : s.ctxParent c ≠ none) :
    s.parC ((s.stk c).headD 0) = some ((s.ctxParent c).getD 0) ∧
    ∀ d, (termEffC s c).Live d → (termEffC s c).ctxParent d =
      if s.ctxParent d = some ((s.stk c).headD 0) then some ((s.ctxParent c).getD 0)
      else s.ctxParent d :=
  ⟨(termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).pf, (termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).par⟩

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6, C6.6; Spec 1 §73 effect): `exitFrameC` changes the kernel
components exactly as the effect of Spec 1 §73 on the view of `c`; reparenting changes only the
contexts, so it creates, elevates, revives and reanchors nothing. -/
theorem exitEffC_kernel (s : SC) (c : Nat) :
    (exitEffC s c).A = (exitEff (s.view c)).A ∧ (exitEffC s c).D = (exitEff (s.view c)).D ∧
    (exitEffC s c).P = s.P ∧ (exitEffC s c).I = s.I ∧ (exitEffC s c).dead = s.dead ∧
    (exitEffC s c).pins = s.pins ∧ (exitEffC s c).nF = s.nF :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6, C7; Spec 1 §73 effect): `terminate` changes the kernel components
exactly as the effect of Spec 1 §73 on the view of `c`. -/
theorem termEffC_kernel (s : SC) (c : Nat) :
    (termEffC s c).A = (exitEff (s.view c)).A ∧ (termEffC s c).D = (exitEff (s.view c)).D ∧
    (termEffC s c).P = s.P ∧ (termEffC s c).I = s.I ∧ (termEffC s c).dead = s.dead ∧
    (termEffC s c).pins = s.pins ∧ (termEffC s c).nF = s.nF :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

end Steps

/-! ## Theorems 2 and 3 for `exitFrameC` and `terminate` -/

section Main

variable {k : K} {s s' : SC} {c : Nat}

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6; Spec 1 §44, §73): an `ok` `exitFrameC` preserves `AnchorOrderC`
(not a precondition of O7) and establishes `AnchorOrderHeldC` (§73.5), with the reparented
initial frames. Fragment: states with the frame structure `FramesC`, `WF3` and `AnchorOrderC`
on the live frames. -/
theorem exitFrameC_anchorOrder (hfr : FramesC s) (hw : WF3 s.flat) (hao : AnchorOrderC s)
    (h : opStepC k .exit c s (.ok s')) : AnchorOrderC s' ∧ AnchorOrderHeldC s' := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hg
  exact ⟨(exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hpre.hasCaller).anchorOrderC hfr hw hao rfl hpre.anchors
    hpre.origins, hpre.anchorOrderHeld⟩

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6, C7; Spec 1 §44, §73): an `ok` `terminate` preserves
`AnchorOrderC` and establishes `AnchorOrderHeldC`, with the reparented initial frames.
Fragment: as `exitFrameC_anchorOrder`. -/
theorem terminate_anchorOrder (hfr : FramesC s) (hw : WF3 s.flat) (hao : AnchorOrderC s)
    (h : TermStep k s c (.ok s')) : AnchorOrderC s' ∧ AnchorOrderHeldC s' := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hg
  have hpar : s.ctxParent c ≠ none := fun e => by
    have := hpre.hasParent; rw [e] at this; exact this
  exact ⟨(termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hpre.initialOnly hpar).anchorOrderC hfr hw hao rfl
    hpre.anchors hpre.origins, hpre.anchorOrderHeld⟩

/-- Theorem 2 for `exitFrameC` (WC2 C6, C20, C23; Spec 1 §57, §73): an `ok` `exitFrameC`
preserves `KInvC` and the auxiliaries `RootHeldConv` and `HeldAnchored` of Spec 1 (not clauses
of §57) on the live frames. Fragment: O7 re-indexed. -/
theorem exitFrameC_preserves (hk : KInvC s) (haux : RootHeldConv s.flat)
    (hh : HeldAnchored s.flat) (h : opStepC k .exit c s (.ok s')) :
    KInvC s' ∧ RootHeldConv s'.flat ∧ HeldAnchored s'.flat := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hg
  have hfr := hk.1.1
  have hp := exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hpre.hasCaller
  exact ⟨hp.kInvC hk (exitEffC_framesC hfr hpre.hasCaller) rfl hpre.anchors hpre.origins
    hpre.anchorOrderHeld, hp.aux hfr haux hh rfl hpre.origins⟩

/-- Theorem 2 for `terminate` (WC2 C7, C20, C23; Spec 1 §57, §73): an `ok` `terminate`
preserves `KInvC` and the auxiliaries `RootHeldConv` and `HeldAnchored` of Spec 1 on the live
frames. -/
theorem terminate_preserves (hk : KInvC s) (haux : RootHeldConv s.flat)

import Ern.Concurrency.Conservativity

/-!
# Reparenting at frame exit and context termination (WC2 C6, C7; OB-C13)

`exitFrameC` (Spec 1 §73 re-indexed with the reparenting of WC2 C6.3) and `terminate` (WC2 C7):

* the frame structure after the step (`FramesC`), and the extended ancestry of the surviving
  frames, which is the ancestry before the step with the exiting frame skipped
  (`exitEffC_ancestorC`, `termEffC_ancestorC`);
* Theorem 3 (OB-C13): both steps preserve `AnchorOrderC` and `AnchorOrderHeldC`, and change `A`
  and `D` exactly as the effect of Spec 1 §73 (`exitEffC_A_D`, `termEffC_A_D`); reparenting
  targets the immediate surviving parent (`exitEffC_reparent`, `termEffC_reparent`);
* Theorem 2 restricted to these steps: `KInvC` and the auxiliaries `RootHeldConv`,
  `HeldAnchored` of Spec 1 on the globally live frames are preserved (`exitFrameC_preserves`,
  `terminate_preserves`).
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

namespace ReparentAux

/-! ## Lists -/

/-- Blockwise sublists give a sublist of the concatenation (WC2 C3). -/
theorem termEffC_ancestorC (hfr : FramesC s) (hone : (s.stk c).length = 1)
    (hpar : s.ctxParent c ≠ none) {g y : Nat} :
    (y ∈ (termEffC s c).frames ↔ y ∈ s.frames ∧ y ≠ (s.stk c).headD 0) ∧
    (g ∈ (termEffC s c).frames → y ∈ (termEffC s c).frames →
      ((termEffC s c).ancestorC g y ↔ s.ancestorC g y)) :=
  ⟨(termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).mem_frames hfr.nodup,
   (termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).ancestorC hfr⟩

/-- WC2 C6.3 (OB-C13): `exitFrameC` reparents exactly the live contexts whose initial frame had
the exiting frame as parent, to the immediate surviving parent of the exiting frame (its caller),
and changes no other parent. -/
theorem exitEffC_reparent (hfr : FramesC s) (hcall : (s.stk c).tail ≠ []) :
    s.parC ((s.stk c).headD 0) = some ((s.stk c).tail.headD 0) ∧
    ∀ d, (exitEffC s c).Live d → (exitEffC s c).ctxParent d =
      if s.ctxParent d = some ((s.stk c).headD 0) then some ((s.stk c).tail.headD 0)
      else s.ctxParent d :=
  ⟨(exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hcall).pf, (exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hcall).par⟩

/-- WC2 C6.3, C7 (OB-C13): `terminate` reparents exactly the live contexts whose initial frame
had the terminated initial frame as parent, to the immediate parent of that frame. -/
theorem termEffC_reparent (hfr : FramesC s) (hone : (s.stk c).length = 1)
    (hpar : s.ctxParent c ≠ none) :
    s.parC ((s.stk c).headD 0) = some ((s.ctxParent c).getD 0) ∧
    ∀ d, (termEffC s c).Live d → (termEffC s c).ctxParent d =
      if s.ctxParent d = some ((s.stk c).headD 0) then some ((s.ctxParent c).getD 0)
      else s.ctxParent d :=
  ⟨(termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).pf, (termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hone hpar).par⟩

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6, C6.6; Spec 1 §73 effect): `exitFrameC` changes the kernel
components exactly as the effect of Spec 1 §73 on the view of `c`; reparenting changes only the
contexts, so it creates, elevates, revives and reanchors nothing. -/
theorem exitEffC_kernel (s : SC) (c : Nat) :
    (exitEffC s c).A = (exitEff (s.view c)).A ∧ (exitEffC s c).D = (exitEff (s.view c)).D ∧
    (exitEffC s c).P = s.P ∧ (exitEffC s c).I = s.I ∧ (exitEffC s c).dead = s.dead ∧
    (exitEffC s c).pins = s.pins ∧ (exitEffC s c).nF = s.nF :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6, C7; Spec 1 §73 effect): `terminate` changes the kernel components
exactly as the effect of Spec 1 §73 on the view of `c`. -/
theorem termEffC_kernel (s : SC) (c : Nat) :
    (termEffC s c).A = (exitEff (s.view c)).A ∧ (termEffC s c).D = (exitEff (s.view c)).D ∧
    (termEffC s c).P = s.P ∧ (termEffC s c).I = s.I ∧ (termEffC s c).dead = s.dead ∧
    (termEffC s c).pins = s.pins ∧ (termEffC s c).nF = s.nF :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

end Steps

/-! ## Theorems 2 and 3 for `exitFrameC` and `terminate` -/

section Main

variable {k : K} {s s' : SC} {c : Nat}

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6; Spec 1 §44, §73): an `ok` `exitFrameC` preserves `AnchorOrderC`
(not a precondition of O7) and establishes `AnchorOrderHeldC` (§73.5), with the reparented
initial frames. Fragment: states with the frame structure `FramesC`, `WF3` and `AnchorOrderC`
on the live frames. -/
theorem exitFrameC_anchorOrder (hfr : FramesC s) (hw : WF3 s.flat) (hao : AnchorOrderC s)
    (h : opStepC k .exit c s (.ok s')) : AnchorOrderC s' ∧ AnchorOrderHeldC s' := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hg
  exact ⟨(exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hpre.hasCaller).anchorOrderC hfr hw hao rfl hpre.anchors
    hpre.origins, hpre.anchorOrderHeld⟩

/-- Theorem 3 (OB-C13; WC2 C6, C7; Spec 1 §44, §73): an `ok` `terminate` preserves
`AnchorOrderC` and establishes `AnchorOrderHeldC`, with the reparented initial frames.
Fragment: as `exitFrameC_anchorOrder`. -/
theorem terminate_anchorOrder (hfr : FramesC s) (hw : WF3 s.flat) (hao : AnchorOrderC s)
    (h : TermStep k s c (.ok s')) : AnchorOrderC s' ∧ AnchorOrderHeldC s' := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hg
  have hpar : s.ctxParent c ≠ none := fun e => by
    have := hpre.hasParent; rw [e] at this; exact this
  exact ⟨(termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hpre.initialOnly hpar).anchorOrderC hfr hw hao rfl
    hpre.anchors hpre.origins, hpre.anchorOrderHeld⟩

/-- Theorem 2 for `exitFrameC` (WC2 C6, C20, C23; Spec 1 §57, §73): an `ok` `exitFrameC`
preserves `KInvC` and the auxiliaries `RootHeldConv` and `HeldAnchored` of Spec 1 (not clauses
of §57) on the live frames. Fragment: O7 re-indexed. -/
theorem exitFrameC_preserves (hk : KInvC s) (haux : RootHeldConv s.flat)
    (hh : HeldAnchored s.flat) (h : opStepC k .exit c s (.ok s')) :
    KInvC s' ∧ RootHeldConv s'.flat ∧ HeldAnchored s'.flat := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg⟩ := h

  have hp := exitEffC_pop hfr.nodup hpre.hasCaller
  exact ⟨hp.kInvC hk (exitEffC_framesC hfr hpre.hasCaller) rfl hpre.anchors hpre.origins
    hpre.anchorOrderHeld, hp.aux hfr haux hh rfl hpre.origins⟩

/-- Theorem 2 for `terminate` (WC2 C7, C20, C23; Spec 1 §57, §73): an `ok` `terminate`
preserves `KInvC` and the auxiliaries `RootHeldConv` and `HeldAnchored` of Spec 1 on the live
frames. -/
theorem terminate_preserves (hk : KInvC s) (haux : RootHeldConv s.flat)
    (hh : HeldAnchored s.flat) (h : TermStep k s c (.ok s')) :
    KInvC s' ∧ RootHeldConv s'.flat ∧ HeldAnchored s'.flat := by
  obtain ⟨-, hg⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hg
  have hfr := hk.1.1
  have hpar : s.ctxParent c ≠ none := fun e => by
    have := hpre.hasParent; rw [e] at this; exact this
  have hp := termEffC_pop hfr.nodup hpre.initialOnly hpar
  exact ⟨hp.kInvC hk (termEffC_framesC hfr hpre.nonInitial hpre.initialOnly hpar) rfl
    hpre.anchors hpre.origins hpre.anchorOrderHeld, hp.aux hfr haux hh rfl hpre.origins⟩

L'agent n'a trouvé aucun problème dans C6 ou C7.

Avec ce module, la compilation passe sans avertissement et les 371 théorèmes `Ern.Concurrency.*` n'utilisent que `{propext, Quot.sound}`.

import Ern.Concurrency.Conservativity
import Ern.Concurrency.SyncLib

/-!
# Preservation of the synchronization invariants (WC2 C21–C23)

Theorem 4 of the brief, preservation half: `SyncInv` (WC2 C21, items 1, 2, 3, 5) and
`GrantDiscipline` (WC2 C22) are preserved by every labelled step `LStep` taken under the
encapsulation hypothesis `Encap` (WC2 C22, C23), together with two auxiliary invariants that are
not WC2 clauses (`GrantSubtree`, `RegBound`). The kernel facts about the states before and after
a step (`KInvC` before, `ConcurrentWF` after) are hypotheses supplied by theorem 2 (preservation of
the re-indexed kernel invariant).

`newMutex` (WC2 C13) registers an entry whose controller (`ControlOf`) need not be a leaf, while

import Ern.Concurrency.Preservation
import Ern.Concurrency.Reparent

/-!
# Theorems 2 and 4 on labelled steps and traces (WC2 C20–C23)

Assembly of `Ern.Concurrency.Preservation`, `Ern.Concurrency.Reparent` and
`Ern.Concurrency.SyncPreserve`:

* theorem 2 for every labelled step of the kernel with the synchronization library
  (`lstep_kInvCA`): `deriveSync` and `acquire` need the own mode `Modify` of `guarded`, which
  `SyncInv` (WC2 C21.1) provides for the library instantiation of `SyncAuthorized`;
* theorems 2 and 4 together along an encapsulated trace (`trace_inv`), and from the initial state
  of Spec 1 §47 with an empty registry (`encapsulated_inv`).
-/

namespace Ern.Concurrency

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- WC2 C21.1: under `SyncInv`, the `guarded` of a live entry has own mode `Modify`. -/
theorem guarded_mode {L : MutexLayout} {s : SC} {reg : SyncReg} {e : SyncEntry}
    (hsi : SyncInv L s reg) (he : e ∈ reg) (hl : e.Live s) :
    OptP (s.A[e.guarded]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify) False := by
  have h := hsi.guarded e he hl
  revert h; unfold OptP
  cases s.A[e.guarded]? with
  | none => exact id
  | some y => exact fun h => h.1

/-- Theorem 2 (WC2 C20, C23) on every labelled step (inherited operations O1–O16 executed by a
context, `spawn`, `terminate`, `join`, `deriveSync` under the library instantiation, `newMutex`,
`acquire`, `unlock`, `resetLock`): the re-indexed kernel invariant with the auxiliaries of Spec 1

Lu comme précondition, la préservation de ces invariants par `spawn` devient vraie par définition (le théorème 2 serait vide pour eux) ; lu comme obligation (convention de Spec 1 §49 dernier alinéa et §58 : la préservation est une propriété requise des transitions), c'est le théorème 2. Même question pour C5.8 (*Preconditions* du composite : « preserves WF3-corresponding requirements, I1–I4, AnchorOrder, AnchorOrderHeld, NoDangling, and NoOrphan ») et C6.5. Formalisé : `SpawnPreBase` (C4.1–C4.5 et la première moitié de C4.6) ; `exitFrameC` suit le brief (O7 + reparentage), C6.5 est traité comme obligation (théorème 3) ; `SpawnValPreBase` sans C5.8.

+**D2. État d'évaluation des préconditions non résultantes du composite par valeur (C5.1, C5.4).** C5.4 fixe l'état final pour les conditions « resulting-state » d'O4, mais pas l'état d'évaluation des autres. Deux en dépendent : le droit du côté source d'O4.1 (C5.1) et l'exemption d'O4.4, parce que la partie `spawn` transfère les paramètres à la nouvelle frame. Exemple concret, vérifié par `decide` (`Transfer.readings_differ`) : frame 0 tient une dérivée `Modify` 3 sur la feuille 0 (sa locale), la transmet au contexte créé et transfère la valeur de la place 0 dans une locale fraîche (place 3) du nouveau contexte. Toutes les clauses de `SpawnValPreBase` sont vraies ; le droit source est vrai avant le composite (par l'autorité 3) et faux après la partie `spawn` (3 est tenue par la nouvelle frame et bloque la racine de la place 0, §43 cas 3). Selon la lecture, le composite est donc `ok` ou `reject`. Lecture (a) : le contexte enfant reçoit à la fois la valeur et une autorité `Modify` sur la feuille source devenue `Moved`. Non formalisé : la relation du composite. Même question, sans divergence constatée (non examinée), pour l'état d'évaluation des conditions résultantes de C4.5–C4.6 dans le composite (après la partie `spawn` ou après le composite).

+**D3. `join` : identifiant inconnu et effet sur `C` (C8).** C8 exige que l'identifiant désigne un contexte connu dont l'état achevé est établi, mais ne donne pas l'issue pour un identifiant inconnu (`reject` ou non habilitée ?) ; il dit que `join` ne modifie pas `P`, `I`, `A`, `D` mais ne dit rien de `C` et `F_C` (un marqueur « joint » est-il prévu ?). Formalisé : seule l'issue `ok` est définie (état inchangé) ; contexte vivant : aucune issue (brief) ; identifiant inconnu : aucune issue, en attente d'arbitrage.

+**D4. Associations de contrôleur distinctes (C12 contre C13).** C12 : « Different mutex instances must have distinct valid controller associations. » Aucune précondition de C13 ne l'assure (C13.7 porte sur l'identité de `guarded`). Avec le `ControlOf` positionnel, deux autorités `guarded` tenues par le même champ (deux racines de stockage possédées par `data`) ont le même contrôleur. Exemple vérifié (`Traces.shared_controller`) : statiques `m = {data, lock}`, `T₁` et `T₂` possédées par `data` ; `newMutex(1)` puis `newMutex(2)` sont acceptés et `ControlOf` vaut `lock` pour les deux entrées. C13.3 (« valid, non-falsifiable association ») le couvre peut-être, mais n'a pas de contenu formel. `SyncInv` ne contient donc pas la distinction des contrôleurs.

+**D5. Clauses sans contenu formel.** Non formalisées, faute de définition : C21.4 (« Registry state and the permitted control operations remain coherent ») ; C13.3 pour « non-falsifiable » ; C13.4 (« Shared observations intended for the controller do not conflict structurally with the protected exclusive authority » : `ctl ∉ footprint(guarded)` serait une lecture) ; C13.6 (« declared appropriately for its mutation discipline » : `K.SharedMutable ctl` serait une lecture) ; C17.5 ; C18.3. C21.3 et C21.5 sont formalisés en lecture minimale explicite : contrôleur positionnel existant, feuille utilisable ; unicité de `guarded` parmi les entrées vivantes (C13.7). C18.4 est une obligation.

+**D6. L'acquisition du contrôleur n'a pas d'effet représentable (C16.1, C17.5).** `S_C` ne porte pas de valeurs (Spec 1 §41 : états d'initialisation seulement) ; l'état « pris/libre » du contrôleur n'existe pas dans `S_C`. Conformément au brief, l'acquisition est représentée par le seul fait d'autorité (`CtrlRight`) et par `grant` dans le registre ; aucun `writeShared` sur le contrôleur n'est effectué par `acquire` ni `unlock`. La correspondance relève d'OB-C05.

+**D7. `GrantDiscipline` n'est pas inductif seul (C22, C23).** `unlock` (C17) libère le grant `g` et pose `grant = none` ; `GrantDiscipline` n'est rétabli que si tout descendant actif de `guarded` couvrant une feuille protégée est `g` ou un descendant de `g` (O3.3 interdit alors tout descendant actif de `g`). Rien dans WC2 ne l'énonce ; C21.4 (« coherent ») le vise peut-être. Formalisé comme auxiliaire `GrantSubtree`. Second auxiliaire, `RegBound` (toute identité `guarded` enregistrée existe) : sans lui, une entrée morte dont l'identité n'existe pas encore deviendrait vivante à la création d'une autorité fraîche de même identité.

+**D9. `deriveSync` perd la borne de mode propre (C15).** Le brief et C15 remplacent `ExercisableAt(source, Modify)` de §60.1 par `SyncAuthorized`. Or `ExercisableAt` porte aussi « le mode propre de `source` permet le mode demandé » ; §60.2 ne borne le mode que feuille par feuille et ne dit rien si le footprint est vide. C15 cite pourtant les « mode restrictions » parmi les exigences conservées. Contre-exemple (`Preservation.deriveSync_breaks_i2`) : état atteignable de Spec 1 où frame 0 dérive de la racine de la statique 0 une autorité 3 `Observe` de footprint vide ; avec un `SyncAuthorized` opaque vrai, `deriveSync(3)` crée une dérivée `Modify` d'une autorité `Observe` et viole I2 (§51). Avec l'instanciation de bibliothèque, `SyncInv` (C21.1) donne le mode `Modify` et la préservation tient (`lstep_kInvCA`). À arbitrer : `DeriveSyncPre` doit-il porter la borne, ou est-ce une obligation de `K_C` (C14 : « correct association with a live synchronization entry ») ?

+**D8. Transposition d'O7.1 (C6, C7).** « The current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller » : C6 parle d'une frame « non-base », mais C3 exige une pile non vide pour tout contexte vivant et C7 traite à part la sortie de la frame initiale d'un contexte. `exitFrameC` est donc défini pour une frame qui a un appelant dans sa propre pile, et `terminate` pour la frame initiale d'un contexte non initial ; C3 et C7 imposent cette lecture, signalée ici parce que C6 ne la formule pas.
+## (e) Décisions de représentation prises ; décisions de conception proposées
+### Prises (aucun programme accepté ni comportement ne change)

+- Contextes : liste indexée par l'identité ; chaque `Ctx` porte sa pile (sommet en tête), son état de cycle de vie et le parent de sa frame initiale (C3 : un seul par contexte). `stk` d'un contexte non vivant est vide.

+- `parC` dérivé des piles et des parents de contextes ; `ancestorC` suit `chain parC` ; le bien-fondé est représenté par l'ordre des identités (`FramesC.parent` : le parent précède l'enfant), conformément à Spec 1 §49 dernier alinéa. Sur les états à un contexte, cela ajoute « pile strictement décroissante » à WF3.1 ; tout état atteignable de Spec 1 la vérifie (`reachable_decreasing`, `reachable_single`).

+- Vues : `SC.view s c` (pile de `c` d'abord, puis les autres frames vivantes) ; Spec 1 §43 ne lit la pile que par son sommet et l'appartenance, et les clauses de §49–§54 seulement par l'appartenance (`wf3_mem_congr` etc.) ; l'ordre des autres frames est donc sans effet sur ces clauses.
+- `SyncAuthorized(state, guarded, requesting_frame)` reçoit la frame : `SC.viewAt` place cette frame au sommet.
+- Les opérations de bibliothèque (`newMutex`, `acquire`, `unlock`, `resetLock`) n'ont qu'une issue `ok` (WC2 n'en définit pas d'autre) ; le blocage est une absence d'issue (brief).

+- Traces : construites directement comme preuves des relations (préconditions décidées par `decide`), sans exécuteur ; un exécuteur sur le patron de `Corpus/Runner.lean` n'était pas nécessaire pour une dizaine de pas.

+- Invariant inductif du théorème 2 : `KInvC` renforcé par les auxiliaires de Spec 1 (`KAux`, `HeldAnchored`) ; invariant inductif du théorème 4 : `SyncInv ∧ GrantDiscipline` renforcé par `GrantSubtree` et `RegBound`. Les énoncés à partir de l'état initial (`encapsulated_inv`) ne les supposent pas.
+### Correction faite pendant le travail

+`NewMutexPreBase.control` exigeait seulement que le `ControlOf` positionnel existe. La preuve du théorème 4 a montré qu'une valeur mutex dont le champ contrôleur n'est pas une feuille passait `newMutex` et violait `SyncInv.control`. C12 dit que `ControlOf` « identifies the synchronization-control leaf » : la clause exige maintenant que le contrôleur soit une feuille (commit ac538af). Ce n'est pas un choix d'interprétation : la version précédente disait moins que C12. `newMutex_nonleaf_rejected` montre l'état concerné : `KInvC` vrai, contrôleur `2` qui n'est pas une feuille, `newMutex` rejeté, et le registre résultant violerait `SyncInv`.
+### Proposées, non prises (`DESIGN.md` ne les règle pas)

+- **P1. `K.Satisfiable` dans le modèle concurrent.** `K` reste inchangé (C2) et `Satisfiable` prend un `S3` ; `alloc` exécuté par `c` l'évalue sur `SC.view s c`. Un `K` arbitraire peut distinguer deux linéarisations : à fixer (vue du contexte exécutant, ou `Satisfiable` sur `S_C` avec projection par l'état à un contexte).

+- **P2. `K_C` instancié par l'état de bibliothèque.** L'instanciation `libKC k L reg` dépend du registre, qui varie le long d'une trace, alors que `K` est un paramètre fixe dans Spec 1. L'obligation de C14 est formalisée par état (`SyncSound kc reg s`). À fixer : `SyncAuthorized` prend-il l'état de bibliothèque en argument ?

+- **P3. Positions déclarées de `ControlOf`.** `MutexLayout` (position du champ tenant `guarded`, position du contrôleur parmi les enfants ordonnés de la valeur mutex) est un paramètre unique de la bibliothèque (un seul type mutex de référence).

+- **P4. Garde unifiée de Spec 1 §56 avec l'arène.** `newMutex` consulte le registre de synchronisation et une liste `adm` d'identités d'autres administrations ; `newArena` de `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena` ne consulte que le registre des arènes. Dans une bibliothèque combinée, `newArena` devrait consulter le registre de synchronisation (§56). Non fait (module Spec 1 inchangé).

+- **P5. Style du jalon 4 de `DESIGN.md`.** Non pris : la sémantique reste relationnelle, sans modèle d'événements, et la question de la forme des contrats sous concurrence (DESIGN.md, *Unsafe contracts*) reste ouverte.
+## (f) Écarts avec la Spec 1

+- Spec 1 §39 et la formalisation de WF3.1 : le bien-fondé des parents de frames est implicite dans la liste. Avec plusieurs piles et des liens entre contextes, il devient une clause explicite (`FramesC.parent`). Sur les états à un contexte, `ancestorC` coïncide exactement avec §39 (`single_ancestorC`), conformément à C3.
+- Spec 1 §58 : seules `ok`, `reject` et `fail` existent. L'attente (C8, C16) n'est pas une issue : c'est une transition non habilitée (brief). `Outcome3` n'est pas étendu.
+- Spec 1 §57, I4 : `Read3Pre` dépend de la frame courante ; I4 ré-indexé est exigé pour chaque contexte (trivial, `i4_always`).

+- Spec 1 §72.3 : la protection d'origine est évaluée avec le nouveau contexte comme contexte exécutant (C4) ; elle ne dit rien de l'exercice par le créateur, protégé seulement par la restriction de `effective` (§43 cas 3), comme C4 le dit.
+- Aucune autre divergence trouvée : les seize opérations ré-indexées ont exactement les issues de Spec 1 sur les états à un contexte (théorème 1).

Tout est commité sur `formal/spec2-m1` avec le rapport `formal/reports/spec2-m1.md`. La compilation passe sans avertissement et les 635 théorèmes de `Ern.Concurrency` n'utilisent que `{propext, Quot.sound}`.

| Théorème | Résultat |
|---|---|
| 1 Conservativité | Prouvé pour O1–O16. Le domaine couvre tout état atteignable de la Spec 1. |
| 2 Préservation | Prouvé pour les 16 opérations héritées, `spawn`, `terminate`, `join` et les opérations de bibliothèque. **Réfuté** pour `deriveSync` tel que défini : contre-exemple (D9). Prouvé seulement si `guarded` est en mode `Modify`. **Ouvert** pour `spawn` par valeur : sa relation n'est pas définie (D2). |
| 3 Reparentage | Prouvé. La cible est le parent immédiat, `A` et `D` sont exactement ceux d'O7, et `AnchorOrderC` est préservé. |
| 4 `SyncInv` et `GrantDiscipline` | Prouvé sous `EncapsulatedTrace`, avec deux invariants auxiliaires nommés (D7). Contre-exemple sans l'hypothèse : le `derive` du propriétaire bloque `acquire` alors que `grant = none`. |
| 5 Réalisabilité | Prouvé, mais il faut aussi l'invariant noyau `KInvC`. Sous `SyncInv ∧ GrantDiscipline` seuls, comme le demandait le brief, l'énoncé est faux : contre-exemple sans I1. |
| 6 Exclusivité des grants | Prouvé. |

Les états accessibles depuis l'état initial par une trace encapsulée satisfont `KInvC`, `SyncInv` et `GrantDiscipline`. Seules hypothèses : `DDSound` et des statiques bien formées.

**Audit des axiomes hérités.** `reachable_kinv` et les 442 théorèmes de `Main` et `Preserve/*` n'utilisent pas `Classical.choice`. Les trois `byContradiction` ne servent qu'à `Rename` et `StaticsConf`, que le jalon 1 ne réutilise pas.

**Problèmes de la candidate** (détail et exemples dans la section (d) du rapport) :
- **D1** : des « invariants » figurent parmi les préconditions de C4.6, C5.8 et C6.5. Lus comme préconditions, ils rendent leur préservation vraie par définition.
- **D2** : le `spawn` par valeur admet deux lectures d'O4.1 et d'O4.4, et un témoin vérifié montre qu'elles divergent : l'une accepte, l'autre rejette.
- **D3** : C8 ne dit pas ce que donne `join` sur un identifiant inconnu.
- **D4** : C12 exige des contrôleurs distincts, mais C13 ne l'assure pas. Témoin : deux mutex sur le même verrou.
- **D5** : plusieurs clauses de C13, C17, C18 et C21 n'ont pas de contenu formel.
- **D9** : remplacer `ExercisableAt` par `SyncAuthorized` fait perdre la borne de mode propre, ce qui casse I2.

**Correction de ma propre formalisation.** `newMutex` n'exigeait pas que le contrôleur soit une feuille, alors que C12 le dit. Un agent l'a découvert pendant sa preuve. Je l'ai corrigé (commit `ac538af`), avec un témoin de l'état concerné.

**Décisions de conception proposées, non prises.** `Satisfiable` évalué sur la vue du contexte exécutant ; `K_C` instancié par le registre de bibliothèque ; positions déclarées de `ControlOf` ; garde unifiée §56 entre `newArena` et le registre de synchronisation.

Les preuves des théorèmes 2 à 4 ont été faites par trois agents en parallèle. J'ai intégré et recompilé leurs modules, puis refait l'audit, sans relire leurs preuves ligne à ligne. Leurs worktrees restent dans `.claude/worktrees/`. Une vérification indépendante des affirmations du rapport contre le code est encore en cours ; je corrigerai le rapport si elle trouve des écarts.

 "mem_movedDeps_part'":'`mem_movedDeps_part` of `Preserve/Transfer.lean`',
 "not_partOf_src'":'`not_partOf_src` of `Preserve/Transfer.lean`',
}
count=0
for i,l in enumerate(lines):
    m=re.match(r"^theorem (\S+)",l)
    if not m: continue
    name=m.group(1)
    if name not in orig: continue
    # search backwards for docstring lines containing 'copy of a private'
    j=i-1
    while j>=0 and not lines[j].startswith('/--'):
        j-=1
    block='\n'.join(lines[j:i])
    if 'copy of a private' not in block: continue
    new=re.sub(r'copy of a private\s+helper( of the [^)]*?)?(?=\))', 'copy of the private '+orig[name], block, flags=re.S)
    new=re.sub(r'copy of a private\s+helper', 'copy of the private '+orig[name], new, flags=re.S)
    if new!=block:
        lines[j:i]=new.split('\n') if False else lines[j:i]
        # replace in place by rebuilding
        s_block_old=block; s_block_new=new
        lines_joined='\n'.join(lines)
        lines_joined=lines_joined.replace(s_block_old,s_block_new,1)
        lines=lines_joined.split('\n')
        count+=1
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
print(count)
EOF

+/-- Equal authority lists have the same skeletons (Spec 1 §42; copy of the private `skel_of_A` of
+`Preserve/Small.lean`). -/
theorem skel_of_A {s s' : S3} (hA : s'.A = s.A) : SameSkel s s' :=
⟨by rw [hA], fun j => by rw [hA]⟩
fun i z hz _ hzo => (hroot i z hzo).2 hz
holders := fun a y hy ya => (HolderLive.congr hP hF hd _).2 (hhold a y hy ya) }
-/-- `I1`–`I4` (Spec 1 §50–§53) carry over to a state with the same places, stack, death markers
-and skeletons, whose anchors of usable places are active (copy of the private `inv3base_skel` of `Preserve/Small.lean`). -/
+/-- `I1`–`I4` (Spec 1 §50–§53) carry over to a state with the same places, stack, death markers and
+skeletons, whose anchors of usable places are active (copy of the private `inv3base_skel` of
+`Preserve/Small.lean`). -/
theorem inv3base_skel {s s' : S3} (hi : Inv3base s) (sk : SameSkel s s')
(hP : s'.P = s.P) (hF : s'.F = s.F) (hd : s'.dead = s.dead)
(hD : ∀ q : Nat, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s'.D q, s.Active x) : Inv3base s' := by
(fun hu => hq ((S3.Usable.congr hP hF hd).2 hu)) l hl (by rw [← e.2.2.1]; exact hly)

-authorities with no origin are authorities of the previous state (copy of the private `rootHeldConv_of` of `Preserve/Small.lean`). -/

+`rootHeldConv_of` of `Preserve/Small.lean`). -/
theorem rootHeldConv_of {s s' : S3} (h : RootHeldConv s) (hP : s'.P = s.P)
(hroot : ∀ (i : Nat) (z : Authority), z.origin = none → s'.A[i]? = some z → s.A[i]? = some z) :

-/-- The effect of `store` on an existing authority (Spec 1 §65 `ok` effect; copy of the private `storeEff_eq` of `Preserve/Small.lean`). -/
+/-- The effect of `store` on an existing authority (Spec 1 §65 `ok` effect; copy of the private

theorem storeEff_eq (hy : t.A[a]? = some y) :
storeEff t a p = { t with
A := t.A.set a { y with holder := .place p }
I := fun l => if l = p then .init else t.I l } := by

(storeEff t a p).A[j]? = if a = j then some { y with holder := .place p } else t.A[j]? := by

        j=i
        while not lines[j].rstrip().endswith('-/'):

        block=lines[i:j+1]
        txt=' '.join(x.strip() for x in block)
        if 'copy of the private' in txt and any(len(x)>100 for x in block):
            body=txt[len('/--'):].strip()
            assert body.endswith('-/')
            body=body[:-2].rstrip()

        else:
            out.extend(block)
        i=j+1
    else:
        out.append(l); i+=1
s='\n'.join(out)
open(p,'w').write(s)
